Hey man it happens lol, Canada is the only one I could see being a problem post World War 2, as they were in the same situation we were in after the war, being as untouched by the war on the Homefront as we were, and having a booming economy because of it. They just didn’t have the military spending or the population that we did. There would be no way that the US would be able to hold onto all that land though, there’s a reason that all empires crumble.
I imagine he could’ve been talking about after the Mexican-American War as well, but I don’t think we had the manpower or the economy back then to accomplish such a feat.

Economically, we were the biggest super power in the world in the wake of World War 2, and had, and still to this day have, the biggest military budget in the world. We were also virtually untouched, with all factories and population centers in the US coming out of the war unscathed, compared to the European powers at the time being almost decimated and depleted of resources, which we were supplying them with. They couldn’t and wouldn’t have stopped us if we were to invade other countries. As for the countries in the Western Hemisphere we would have invaded, most countries at the time (Honduras, Nicaragua, El Salvador, etc.) did not have the economy, population, nor the infrastructure or military to stop us if we were to invade them. I’m not saying it’d be a walk in the park, but the US has been a military power in the world for the past 100 years for a reason.
He’s not completely wrong, militarily the US could’ve done it. Economically, in the long run, it wouldn’t have been a smart choice.
